justifications.functional_suitability: The Scoring Engine handles R-01 (approve/decline/review decisions), the Case Management API and Fraud Analyst SPA satisfy R-02 (case management), and the Rule & Model Distribution Service handles R-03 (zero-downtime rule and model updates).
justifications.performance_efficiency: The sub-50ms P99 target at 3k TPS is supported by in-memory Go evaluation, ElastiCache Redis feature lookups, ALB termination, and asynchronous EventBridge dispatch. However, EventBridge PutEvents throughput default limits and single-event calls at 3,000 TPS may introduce latency overhead unless batched.
justifications.compatibility: The Payment Gateway connects over HTTPS/gRPC via Payment Ingress Router, while Card Networks/Tokenization Service and external ML providers are represented. Explicit token exchange flows with external tokenization services are slightly abstract at lower levels.
justifications.usability: Fraud Analysts are thoroughly supported by Fraud Analyst SPA, featuring dedicated components like Case Review Workspace Module, Explainability Renderer, and Analytics Dashboard Module to review payments and inspect explainability metrics.
justifications.reliability: Circuit breaking in Scoring API Controller and DLQs in Asynchronous Event Bus handle failures. However, an explicit fallback mechanism ensuring payments are not blocked for over 1 minute during complete scoring failure (R-07) lacks clear architectural specification.
justifications.security: Strong PCI-DSS alignment: PAN token stripping in Scoring API Controller, mTLS, AWS Cognito with JWT, KMS Ed25519 bundle signing, Row-Level Security, SHA-256 cryptographic chaining in Audit Ledger Writer, and S3 Glacier Object Lock for WORM storage.
justifications.maintainability: Clean domain separation across containers and components (Rule Syntax Linter, Feature Aggregator, Audit Dispatcher). However, supporting three distinct runtimes (Go, Python/FastAPI, Java/Spring) may place high operational burden on a 3-engineer team.
justifications.portability: Effectively targets AWS eu-west-1 using ECS Fargate, Aurora, and ElastiCache. Heavy reliance on proprietary AWS managed primitives (Cognito, EventBridge, S3 Glacier WORM) slightly impairs portability, but matches target cloud constraints well.

PERF-01.justification: In-memory rule execution and asynchronous event-driven audit dispatching avoid blocking the critical path, but synchronous AWS KMS signing and EventBridge PutEvents at 3,000 TPS risk tail-latency spikes without explicit local batching.
sensitivity_points: AWS KMS signing latency in the synchronous scoring path
ElastiCache Redis read latency under 3,000 TPS concurrent load
tradeoffs: Synchronous cryptographic signing ensures non-repudiation at the expense of tail latency

PERF-02.justification: Scoring and case management are completely decoupled across separate ingress routes, independent Fargate containers, and distinct data tiers with read replicas and caching, ensuring analyst queries cannot degrade scoring throughput.
sensitivity_points: Aurora read-replica replication lag during high write volume
Network isolation between scoring ALB and management API Gateway
tradeoffs: Using read replicas improves analyst query latency while introducing brief data staleness

AVAIL-01.justification: While the Scoring API Controller includes circuit breaking, there is no defined standalone fallback decider or gateway stand-in mechanism to render and audit fallback decisions when the Scoring Engine container itself crashes.
sensitivity_points: Absence of edge-level stand-in processing when scoring service is unavailable
Health-check reaction time and failover routing at the ALB
tradeoffs: Failing fast protects downstream resources but leaves payment approval fallback unhandled

AVAIL-02.justification: The scoring path streams audit records asynchronously to Amazon EventBridge, backed by SQS dead-letter queues and event archiving, buffering records without impacting scoring latency or risking data loss if Aurora degrades.
sensitivity_points: SQS dead-letter queue retention limits during prolonged database downtime
tradeoffs: Asynchronous audit decoupling guarantees scoring availability but creates eventual consistency for audit persistence

MOD-01.justification: The distribution service delivers cryptographically signed bundles to S3, and the Scoring Engine uses atomic in-memory pointer swaps to hot-reload models instantly with zero downtime and fast rollback, while recording model versions in payloads.
sensitivity_points: Memory footprint of maintaining dual model versions during pointer swap
Background polling intervals for rule/model bundle updates
tradeoffs: Atomic pointer swapping enables zero-downtime hot reloading at the cost of transient memory overhead

MOD-02.justification: The architecture incorporates automated rule linting, KMS bundle signing, and hot-reload synchronization without downtime well within the one-hour window, with decision outputs capturing rule IDs for explainability.
sensitivity_points: Correctness of rule AST validation before cryptographic signing
Propagation latency of new rule bundles from S3 to engine instances
tradeoffs: Strict rule pre-compilation and validation delays deployment slightly but eliminates runtime evaluation crashes

SEC-01.justification: Card data is tokenized externally and stripped before reaching analyst applications, fulfilling the zero clear-text PAN requirement. However, the architecture lacks explicit intrusion detection or anomaly monitoring mechanisms to alert on compromised analyst behavior within 15 minutes.
sensitivity_points: Tokenization boundary enforcement prior to case database ingestion
Absence of real-time behavioral anomaly alerting for analyst accounts
tradeoffs: Tokenization drastically shrinks PCI scope but shifts identity security entirely to IAM/Cognito controls

SEC-02.justification: Audit payloads with inputs, model IDs, and explanations are cryptographically chained with SHA-256 in Aurora and archived to AWS S3 Glacier with WORM Object Lock for 7 years, retrievable within hours via the Audit Query Gateway.
sensitivity_points: Integrity verification of SHA-256 cryptographic chain across archived partitions
S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval retrieval job latency
tradeoffs: Tiering historical audit logs to Glacier reduces costs but introduces hours-long retrieval latency
